erin_sec: Heads-up: assembling a tight hardening pass for PrivatePod deploys. Focus: deny-by-default netpols, precise RBAC for keystore SA, richer decrypt audit fields, and a low-risk vuln patch flow. Thoughts?

sam_infra: Important: do not open outbound 443. Allow only kube-dns and the specific HSM CIDRs and OCSP hostnames. We'll provide a model netpol.

jo_ops: Logging request: include `caller_sa`, `pod_uid`, `kms_request_id`, and `hsm_status` on every decrypt entry. We lost traceability last sprint because `pod_uid` was missing.

mike_devsec: RBAC approach: remove any wildcard bindings in the privedge cluster. Create a Role `keystore-client` scoped to namespace `keystore` granting just `create` on `secrets/keystore-requests` and `get` on `pods`. I'll drop a YAML.

erin_sec: For the vulnerability in the sidecar, propose: build patched image, run `./tests/kms_smoke --n=500` against HSM simulator, then canary to one private pool AZ with identical netpols. If error rate >0.3% revert.

sam_infra: Canary caveat: ensure canary pod uses same egress whitelist and mesh routes. Different egress caused false positives previously.

jo_ops: Alert rule suggestion: `sum(rate(kms_decrypt_errors[5m])) / sum(rate(kms_decrypt_requests[5m])) > 0.003` -> P1, switch traffic to hosted fallback, open incident.

mike_devsec: Also ensure audit logs export `kms_req_id` as a tag for SIEM mapping. Jo, can you map fields to the onprem index?

jo_ops: Yes, I'll map `kms_request_id` -> `kms.request_id`, `hsm_status` -> `hsm.status_code`. Retention ask: 90d hot, archive 2y. I'll follow up with compliance.

erin_sec: Action items: mike -> RBAC PR, sam -> netpol + canary manifest, jo -> SIEM mapping + alert rule. Sync tomorrow 09:00 PT. :thumbsup:
